reason: Wonderschool's live Head of Engineering posting says the role must build "the high-performing engineering organization that can ship reliable, scalable products and fully leverage these systems" while a parallel live Head of AI Agent Systems req describes a multi-agent system already running ops - a company whose high-touch human-delivered childcare services are being converted into an AI-backed product with no engineering leader in place, which is exactly Daniel's stated niche.

company.name: Wonderschool
company.one_liner: AI-powered marketplace, SaaS and government-infrastructure platform that helps childcare providers launch and operate programs and helps states manage subsidy, licensing and payment-integrity programs.
company.stage: Series B (~$49M raised; a16z, Goldman Sachs, First Round, Long Journey; described as cash flow positive in its own JD); ~80-133 employees
company.hq: 548 Market Street, San Francisco, CA, USA

evidence_jobs.title: Head of Engineering
evidence_jobs.quote: The Head of Engineering is responsible for building the high-performing engineering organization that can ship reliable, scalable products and fully leverage these systems.

evidence_jobs.title: Head of AI Agent Systems
evidence_jobs.quote: A core part of our strategy is using AI to automate how work gets done across the company. This includes product development, operations, customer support, and go-to-market. ... We have already deployed a multi-agent system using OpenClaw and our internal Claude Code system.

evidence_jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Applied AI
evidence_jobs.quote: OpenClaw agents run most of our operations: provider outreach, customer communications, enrollment workflows, compliance tasks. ... We are now taking the next step: making AI agents reliable enough to build the product itself.

people_spec: Chief Executive Officer / Co-Founder (the AI Product Support Lead req states the role reports directly to the CEO, and the Head of Engineering hire is open - the CEO currently owns engineering)
Chief Product Officer / VP Product (Product Managers for Government Platform, Payments and Growth are being hired under this function)
Head of AI Agent Systems (open req - if filled, this is the peer who inherits the verification load)
Chief of Staff to the CEO
talk_track: I've spent the last few years moving work that lived in people's hands into AI systems that hold up under real load - most recently running platform and reliability engineering at Tricentis, where agents for incident detection and on-call cut MTTR by about 40%. Your Head of Engineering posting says the role is "responsible for building the high-performing engineering organization that can ship reliable, scalable products and fully leverage these systems," and it sits next to an open Head of AI Agent Systems req describing a multi-agent system already running provider outreach, enrollment and compliance. Read together, those two postings describe a harder problem than either one alone: the agents are already in production, so the constraint has moved from building them to verifying them. Most teams at that point hire more implementers, and the verification load quietly outgrows the org - it shows up as agent output nobody has capacity to check, not as missed sprints. What has worked for me is funding an evaluation harness and a delivery cadence before the next headcount, so cost-to-deliver stops tracking headcount one-for-one. Is verification capacity anyone's job there yet? - Daniel Kirichanski, Prime Path Global
